results.title: Errors and exceptions · Cloudflare Workers docs
results.content:
### Validation Errors (10021)

The 10021 error code includes all errors that occur when you attempt to deploy a Worker, and Cloudflare then attempts to load and run the top-level scope (everything that happens before your Worker's handler is invoked). For example, if you attempt to deploy a broken Worker with invalid JavaScript that would throw a `SyntaxError` — Cloudflare will not deploy your Worker.

Specific error cases include but are not limited to:

#### Script startup exceeded CPU time limit

This means that you are doing work in the top-level scope of your Worker that takes more than the startup time limit (1s) of CPU time.

#### Script startup exceeded memory limit [...] | Error code | Meaning |
 --- |
| `1101` | Worker threw a JavaScript exception. |
| `1102` | Worker exceeded CPU time limit. |
| `1103` | The owner of this worker needs to contact Cloudflare Support |
| `1019` | Worker hit loop limit. |
| `1021` | Worker has requested a host it cannot access. |
| `1022` | Cloudflare has failed to route the request to the Worker. |
| `1024` | Worker cannot make a subrequest to a Cloudflare-owned IP address. |
| `1027` | Worker exceeded free tier daily request limit. |
| `1042` | Worker tried to fetch from another Worker on the same zone, which is only supported when the `global_fetch_strictly_public` compatibility flag is used. Also returned for a `workers.dev` URL with no Worker serving it, such as a Worker with its `workers.dev` route disabled. | [...] In Cloudflare Workers, each invocation is handled independently and has its own execution context. This design ensures optimal performance and security by isolating requests from one another. When you try to share I/O objects between different invocations, you break this isolation. Since these objects are tied to the specific request they were created in, accessing them from another request's handler is not allowed and leads to the error.

This error is most commonly caused by attempting to cache an I/O object, like a Request in global scope, and then access it in a subsequent request. results.title: Cloudflare Workers: Unpacking My Fundamental Misunderstanding - DEV Community
results.content:
That implied either of two things:

 Cloudflare has a bug in their “beta” Queues Workers product
 My fundamental knowledge and assumptions about Cloudflare Workers have been wrong for years since their introduction.

After a brief conversation in their Discord channel and with the Director of Product for Cloudflare Workers, I learnt that my understanding had been wrong.

I had believed that every Worker invocation is executed in a completely isolated environment, with a new V8 isolate created for each call and discarded right after the call is finished. This assumption led me to think that there was no need to worry about possible data leaks between calls, a problem inherent in most (all?) serverless platforms. This feature was one of the primary reasons I was excited about Workers.

results.title: workers.dev NXDOMAIN for all workers incl. newly created ones - Developers / Cloudflare Workers - Cloudflare Community
results.content:
Mid-outage I created a brand-new Worker via the API. The deploy succeeded, but its .workers.dev hostname returned HTTP 404 with Cloudflare error 1042 — and a random nonexistent hostname under my account subdomain returned the same 1042. So this was account-subdomain-wide, not tied to my Workers’ code or config.
   The dashboard and API showed everything healthy the entire time: deploys succeeding, Workers Active, zero errors, no billing or account flags.
   DNS was strange rather than cleanly broken: at one point the authoritative nameserver answered NOERROR with zero records (not NXDOMAIN), while 1.1.1.1 resolved even nonexistent names under the subdomain to Cloudflare anycast IPs. The failure presented as edge hostname routing (1042). [...] ### .

This looks like workers.dev hostname provisioning/serving is broken for my account subdomain while the Workers control plane stays healthy. I’m on the free plan so I can’t open a technical support case — posting here per the dashboard’s guidance. Happy to provide dig outputs and timestamps.
